texts.orig: We wonder whether the results of this section are valid when restricting to fams with the uap. These are not in general. For example, let a ⊆ ω be the set of even numbers, B := P ( ω ), let B 0 be the field of sets over ω generated by a and let F ⊆ P ( ω ) be the filter of subsets of ω containing { 0 , 1 } . Let Ξ 0 be the (unique) probability measure on B such that Ξ( a ) = 2 3 (which is clearly uniformly supported). By Theorem 3.15, there is a unique probability fam Ξ on 〈 B 0 ∪ F 〉 extending Ξ 0 such that Ξ( b ) = 1 for all b ∈ F , in particular, Ξ( { 0 , 1 } ) = 1. Then, Ξ( { 0 } ) = Ξ( a ∩ { 0 , 1 } ) = Ξ 0 ( a ) = 2 3 and, naturally, Ξ( { 1 } ) = 1 3 . However, Ξ cannot have the uap because no singleton can have measure 2 3 under a probability fam with the uap (by Theorem 2.18). This also shows that Theorem 3.8 is not valid in general when restricting to the uap: both Ξ 0 and Ξ F are uniformly supported, but any common extension extends Ξ and thus cannot have the uap.

texts.orig: Proof. If all finite sets have Ξ 0 -measure zero, then the same is true for Ξ. So assume that Ξ 0 is uniformly supported with support P . Since B 0 contains all finite sets, all finite sets in P with positive measure must be singletons (by minimality). It is not hard to show that P is a support of Ξ, so Ξ is uniformly supported. □ 3 . 16

texts.orig: Question 3.18. Assume that B 0 and B 1 are fields of sets over X , containing all the singletons, and Ξ 0 and Ξ 1 are uniformly supported fams with the uap on B 0 and B 1 , respectively. Assume that Ξ 0 and Ξ 1 are compatible (in the sense of Theorem 3.8 (iii) ). Is there a uniformly supported fam that extends both Ξ 0 and Ξ 1 ?
